name: Turkey Manicotti with Ricotta
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Verified 6 servings, 525 cal, 41g protein straight off the source, so the calorie and protein gates are met without any scaling. Stuffed tubes are more assembly than a pure skillet, but it is a one-pan bake and portions two-per-serving, which stays sane at 14. Distinct from baked ziti and stuffed shells in the catalog by shape and filling. | HARVEST:
intro_html: Manicotti is the Sunday dinner shape: big pasta tubes stuffed with ricotta and meat, buried in marinara, blanketed in mozzarella. It takes more assembly than a skillet dish, but every minute of it happens once and then feeds you for two weeks. Each serving carries {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein for about ${{cost_ps}} (at everyday cost).
ingredients_display: Pasta Shells - jumbo (Great Value): 19.5 oz dry (552 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pasta Shells - jumbo, 19.5 oz dry: ~$4.61. Buy 2 Great Value 12 ozes: $5.69.
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper, italian seasoning): ~$0.13. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $31.98 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.28 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $38.73 across 14 servings, roughly $2.77 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $15.58 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $54.31. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a container (at everyday cost). Stuffed pasta at a red sauce restaurant starts around eighteen dollars and does not come with a second helping waiting in your fridge.
shop_smart: The jumbo shells are the biggest single line on this list. Watch for the store brand, which usually runs half the Barilla price for a shape that gets stuffed and covered in sauce anyway.
Ricotta is the heart of the filling and the 15 ounce tubs are the value size. Three of them cover this batch and the leftover ounces go straight into scrambled eggs or toast.

Fresh basil costs about the price of a candy bar for one small pack. That is the right amount to spend. Dried basil is not the same thing here, since the fresh leaf is what cuts the richness of all that cheese.
Buy mozzarella in 8 ounce bags on sale and freeze the extras. Shredded cheese freezes better than almost anything else in the dairy case and it goes straight from freezer to pan.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the jumbo shells to just under done, about 2 minutes short of the box, then drain and spread them out so they do not stick together while you work.

Heat the olive oil, cook the diced onion 5 minutes, add the garlic for a minute, then brown the ground turkey until it is cooked through to 165F. Season with the italian seasoning, salt, and pepper and let it cool a few minutes.
Mix the ricotta with the chopped fresh basil and about a third of the mozzarella, then fold in the cooled turkey. Cool matters, because hot meat turns ricotta runny.
Spread a layer of marinara across the bottom of your baking pans so nothing sticks.
Stuff each shell with the filling using a spoon or a zip bag with the corner cut off, then set them in the pans in rows.
Cover with the rest of the marinara and the remaining mozzarella, then bake covered at 375F for 30 minutes, uncover, and bake 10 more until the top browns.
Rest 15 minutes before you portion, then divide the stuffed shells and sauce evenly among the containers.
portion_html: Set the pot of rice on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. That is the base in each container. Then divide the stuffed shells evenly by count across all 14 and spoon the extra sauce from the pan over the top. Each serving lands at {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein.

recipeIngredient: Pasta Shells - jumbo, 19.5 oz dry (552 g)
steps: Boil the jumbo shells 2 minutes short of done and drain.
Cook onion and garlic in olive oil, brown the ground turkey to 165F, season, and let it cool.
Mix ricotta with basil, part of the mozzarella, and the cooled turkey.
Spread marinara in the pans, stuff the shells, and arrange them in rows.
Top with remaining marinara and mozzarella and bake covered at 375F for 30 minutes, then 10 uncovered.
Rest 15 minutes, then divide the stuffed shells and sauce evenly among the 14 containers.
